structural_answer: The breaker fired on 'each round's new safety mechanism is itself unbound'. This round adds no checker-per-mechanism. It binds the two mechanisms round 2 left unbound, and every binding was mutated before it was claimed — seven mutations, seven RED, restore GREEN, transcript in part 2. The one result that does not read as cleanly as the others is stated rather than smoothed: reverting rung 2's cap turns the CI unit-tests job red and leaves the eval suite at 79/79.

findings.fix: The tier record carries `offset`, and the strip renders the true range — 'saw chars 178,087–238,087, not the whole document' instead of 'the first 60,000 chars'. `specs/001` documents `offset` beside `input_chars`/`truncated` and states the three are one fact: a RANGE into normalized_text. `_routing_shape` requires all three together and additionally checks the range lies inside the document and that `truncated` agrees with the arithmetic — so it binds every producer, not just the one that noticed.
findings.why_a_length_was_not_enough: rung 1's window starts at the largest unattributed region. On 18 of 43 dev documents that is not 0; on axp-2008 it is 178,087 and on bac-2006 663,941. A length alone cannot express what was read, so the screen stated a falsehood the envelope could not even contradict.

findings.fix: `check_escalation_locks` now pins the arming SEMANTICS: exactly one `Eq` operator against the literal ADR-036 §h2 names, not any Compare over the right name. And a new `_default_of` — the mirror of `_env_get`, which deliberately steps OVER the `or` operand and is exactly how an unbounded default slipped through — requires each ceiling's fallback to be a plain numeric literal inside (0, cap]. `DEFAULT_CEILINGS` sizes those caps at the published defaults with headroom, so raising a default stays possible and unbounding it does not.

ci_failure.state: the branch was RED on CI at 9f43429; unit-tests failed while invariant-eval and fast-eval passed
ci_failure.how_it_escaped_my_verification: I checked every self-check with `python3 -m <mod> 2>&1 | tail -1` and read the output. `$?` after a pipe is the EXIT STATUS OF `tail`, which is always 0, so a module that raised printed its traceback into the middle of the piped output and still reported as '[PASS] test_confidence' on the last line. The verification could not fail — which is the same defect class this PR spent four rounds fixing, committed by the person fixing it. Every self-check in this repair is confirmed by EXIT CODE, unpiped.
ci_failure.symptom: KeyError: 'method' at eval_adapter.py:241 in eval_check, via test_envelope_shape
ci_failure.root_cause_chosen: the guard belongs in eval_check — specifically, in its ORDERING
ci_failure.why_that_one: `specs/001` does require `method` on every item, so the synthetic envelope is a contract violation. But that is precisely what `test_envelope_shape` exists to construct: its deletion loop hands `envelope_shape` an envelope missing each required item field in turn and asserts the checker REPORTS it. `eval_check`'s job is judging malformed envelopes; crashing on one is not judging it, and 'fixing' the fixture by adding `method` back would have deleted the only check that `envelope_shape` catches a missing `method` — papering over a contract violation the checker should be catching, which is the failure mode the finding names.
ci_failure.fix: One block move, not a tolerance patch. The `routing` cross-check block introduced in round 1 sat among the optional-key shape checks, ABOVE the per-item key/enum loop and above the trace/timings/cost shape check — so it read `i['method']` and `result['cost'][...]` before either had been validated. It now runs LAST in the branch: validate shape, then cross-check honesty. No `.get()` was added and no violation is newly tolerated — a missing `method` is still rejected, now with the contract message `item 1 missing ['method']` instead of a traceback.

sibling_audit.method: AST sweep of every string subscript in the escalation code this PR added (_routing_shape, escalate.trigger/_windows/verify/apply), each checked against whether a guard precedes it, then confirmed by running the mutation.
found_and_fixed_by_the_same_move: _routing_shape's `by_tier = {i['item'] ... if i['method'] in ESCALATION_METHODS}` — same unvalidated `method` read; now after the item loop.

_routing_shape's `result['cost'][k]` — read before the trace/timings/cost shape check that validates those keys. Verified: an envelope with routing and an empty `cost` now returns 'trace/timings/cost not in contract shape' instead of KeyError.
audited_and_safe: escalate.trigger — `w['code']`/`w['message']` iterate `hits`, already filtered by `w.get('code') in TRIGGER_CODES`; `w['item']` is gated by `and w.get('item')` in the same comprehension.

escalate.verify / apply — the risky reads already use `.get()` (`i.get('start')`, `it.get('evidence')`); the rest run on items `extract.py` constructed one call earlier, not on caller-supplied envelopes.
_routing_shape's `r[...]`, `t[...]`, `tier[...]` — each preceded by its own `<required set> <= set(...)` membership guard.
found_and_deliberately_not_fixed: `eval_check`'s opening `by_code = {i['item']: i for i in result.get('items', [])}` (eval_adapter.py:70) crashes for EVERY check type on an item missing `item`. Same class, but pre-existing dispatcher code — not escalation code, not added by this PR — and `test_envelope_shape`'s deletion loop does not cover the `item` key. Carried as a debt row in tasks/TODO.md rather than widened into a CI-red fix being amended into an already-reviewed commit.
